timeline.title: How Our Favourite Traditions Began
items: In Strasbourg, fir trees were set up indoors and hung with paper roses, apples and sweets.
Henry Cole sent the first printed Christmas card. That same year, Dickens wrote A Christmas Carol.
London sweet maker Tom Smith wrapped sweets in twists of paper. Later he added the famous bang.
On the Western Front, soldiers sang carols, swapped gifts and played football in no man's land.
today: Not in the history books yet. But the best Christmas tradition we know is you.

letters.title: What the World Has Said About Christmas
items: I will honour Christmas in my heart, and try to keep it all the year.
Christmas won't be Christmas without any presents.
Maybe Christmas, he thought, doesn't come from a store.
Dr. Seuss, How the Grinch Stole Christmas!
At Christmas play and make good cheer, for Christmas comes but once a year.
letters.hand: They all say it beautifully. We just say: Merry Christmas, {who}.

facts.title: The Secret History of Christmas
items: The very first tinsel was made in Germany from thin strips of real silver.
In 1965, astronauts played Jingle Bells on a harmonica, the first song performed in space.
Rudolph was created in 1939 for a free colouring book handed out by a department store.
A misprinted phone number in a 1955 advert led to the famous tradition of tracking Santa.
Mince pies once really were filled with meat, mixed with dried fruit and spices.
A picture of Queen Victoria's family round a tree in 1848 made Christmas trees hugely popular.
facts.hand: History can explain a lot. It still cannot explain who ate the last chocolate.

world.kicker: A thank you from all of us
world.title: Why Christmas Is Better With You
items: A table full of laughter and second helpings.
The best worst jokes, read out loud.
Someone to share the last roast potato with.
Board games we will argue about for years.
Hugs warm enough to melt the snow.
And a home we always want to come back to.
world.close: Christmas is better because of you, {who}. Ours most of all.

promises.title: Our Christmas promises
items: To wear the paper hat, every year.
To leave one mince pie for Santa.
To laugh at every single cracker joke.
To be home for Christmas, whatever it takes.
To love you, always, all year round.

note.title: What we believe Christmas is
paras: We make magazines for a living, and every December we get a little giddy. This one made us smile.
We believe Christmas is not the presents or the perfect table. It is the paper hats, the burnt bits, the jokes nobody laughs at, and everyone you love squeezed into one warm room.
{who}, someone wanted your Christmas kept forever. Not a card that ends up in a drawer, but pages full of you: your traditions, your chaos, your love.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, your Christmas is the best one going.
note.wish: Merry Christmas, {who}. Here is to many more.
